subject: bumblebee
title: A Fly Turns a Bumblebee Into a Zombie That Digs Its Own Grave

scenes.text: A bumblebee digs a hole, climbs in, and buries itself. It didn't choose to.
Days earlier, a conopid fly ambushed it in mid-air and slipped an egg inside its body.
The maggot eats the bee from the inside for about twelve days. The bee keeps working anyway.
In one study, about seventy percent of infected bees of two species dug into the soil before dying.
Why? A buried bee makes a sheltered tomb, where the fly can spend the winter safe underground.
Next summer, a fly climbs out of that grave and goes hunting bumblebees.

description:
Conopid flies ambush bumblebees in flight and lay an egg inside them; the larva eats the bee from within for about 12 days.
Before dying, many parasitised bees bury themselves in soil (about 70% in two species in a 2014 Animal Behaviour study), giving the fly pupa a protected place to overwinter.
Have you ever seen a bee digging into the ground?
thumbnail_text: FLY MAKES BEE DIG ITS GRAVE
first_comment: Brown-belted bumblebees fight back: they kill about 30% of the larvae inside them by walling them off. Which parasite creeps you out the most?
